title: Ebola Outbreak Reaches Grim Milestone of 10,000 Cases
subtitle: Health officials struggle to contain the fastest-spreading Ebola crisis in history as it moves across borders.

summary.en: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has officially surpassed 10,000 cases. This is the fastest-spreading Ebola crisis ever recorded. Health experts are worried because the virus is a rare type that currently lacks an approved vaccine. The disease has now moved beyond Congo, with cases reported in Kenya and Nigeria. Authorities are calling for stronger international cooperation to stop the spread.
summary.zh: 剛果民主共和國的伊波拉疫情病例數已正式突破一萬大關，這是史上擴散速度最快的伊波拉危機。衛生專家感到擔憂，因為該病毒屬於罕見類型，目前缺乏核准的疫苗。疾病現已蔓延至剛果境外，肯亞與奈及利亞皆有通報病例。當局正呼籲加強國際合作以遏止疫情擴散。

paragraphs.en: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached a sad and serious milestone. According to government figures, more than 10,000 people have been infected since the crisis began in May. This makes it the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak in history. While the 2014-2016 outbreak in West Africa had a higher total number of cases, health officials noted that the current situation is moving much faster and covering a larger geographic area.
paragraphs.zh: 剛果民主共和國的伊波拉病毒疫情已達到一個令人遺憾且嚴峻的里程碑。根據政府數據，自五月危機爆發以來，已有超過一萬人受到感染。這使其成為歷史上擴散速度最快的伊波拉疫情。儘管二零一四至二零一六年間西非的疫情總病例數較多，但衛生官員指出，目前的情況惡化速度更快，且影響的地理範圍更廣。

paragraphs.en: According to the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, the virus has already spread to five countries, including Kenya and Nigeria. In Kenya, officials confirmed nine infections and two deaths after a patient traveled from the Democratic Republic of Congo through Uganda. Meanwhile, Nigeria reported an infection in a diplomat's wife who had recently visited Uganda. These cases show how easily the virus can cross borders, making it a major concern for the entire continent.
paragraphs.zh: 根據非洲疾病管制暨預防中心（Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention）的資料，病毒已擴散至包括肯亞與奈及利亞在內的五個國家。在肯亞，官員證實有九起感染病例與兩起死亡案例，起因是一名病患從剛果民主共和國經由烏干達入境。同時，奈及利亞通報了一起外交官夫人的感染病例，她近期曾造訪烏干達。這些案例顯示病毒跨越國界是多麼容易，這已成為整個非洲大陸的主要隱憂。

paragraphs.en: One of the biggest challenges is that this outbreak is caused by a rare type of the virus called Bundibugyo. Unlike other types of Ebola, there is currently no approved vaccine or specific treatment for this version. Medical teams are working on clinical trials to see if existing vaccines might provide protection, but these tests are still in the early stages. The lack of a proven way to stop the virus makes it much harder for doctors to save lives.
paragraphs.zh: 目前面臨的最大挑戰之一，在於此次疫情是由一種名為「本迪布焦」（Bundibugyo）的罕見病毒株所引起。與其他類型的伊波拉病毒不同，目前針對此版本尚無核准的疫苗或特定療法。醫療團隊正致力於臨床試驗，以觀察現有疫苗是否能提供保護力，但這些測試仍處於早期階段。缺乏證實有效的防疫手段，使得醫師在挽救生命時面臨極大困難。

paragraphs.en: Experts say that the virus likely started spreading months before it was officially identified in May. This delay gave the disease time to move through remote areas where conflict and poor roads already made it difficult for help to arrive. Nahid Bhadelia, an infectious disease physician at Boston University, noted that international cooperation has been slower this time compared to previous outbreaks. She explained that some healthcare workers from other countries are hesitant to join the response due to strict policies about returning home if they become sick. As a result, local health workers are carrying most of the burden.
paragraphs.zh: 專家表示，病毒很可能在五月正式被識別前，就已經擴散了數個月。這段延誤讓疾病有時間在偏遠地區蔓延，而當地原本就因衝突與道路狀況不佳，導致救援難以抵達。波士頓大學（Boston University）傳染病醫師娜希德·巴德利亞（Nahid Bhadelia）指出，與過去的疫情相比，此次國際合作的腳步較為緩慢。她解釋說，部分來自其他國家的醫護人員因擔心染病後返國的嚴格政策，對於投入防疫工作感到猶豫。結果，大部分的重擔都落在當地醫護人員身上。

paragraphs.en: Beyond the medical challenges, health teams are fighting against fear and misinformation. In many communities, people are skeptical of medical staff, and some have even become violent toward those trying to help. Sephora Bgosi, who works with a burial team in the Ituri province, said that some people still do not understand how dangerous the virus is. This lack of trust is a major barrier to survival. According to the Africa CDC, about 80% of new cases are coming from outside of monitored contacts. This means the virus is spreading in ways that health authorities cannot yet track or control.
paragraphs.zh: 除了醫療挑戰外，衛生團隊還必須對抗恐懼與錯誤資訊。在許多社區中，民眾對醫護人員抱持懷疑態度，有些人甚至對試圖提供協助的人員施加暴力。在伊圖里省（Ituri）負責遺體處理團隊的塞芙拉·波戈西（Sephora Bgosi）表示，有些人仍不了解病毒的危險性。這種信任的缺失是生存的一大障礙。根據非洲疾病管制暨預防中心統計，約有百分之八十的新增病例來自監控名單之外。這意味著病毒正以衛生當局尚未能追蹤或控制的方式擴散。

paragraphs.en: Despite these difficulties, there have been some moments of hope. At least 2,600 patients have recovered from the disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo. A recent video showed health workers dancing as the last two patients were discharged from a treatment center in Ituri province. World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said that while the outbreak is far from over, every life saved is worth celebrating.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管困難重重，仍有一些令人振奮的時刻。在剛果民主共和國，至少已有兩千六百名病患康復。近期一段影片顯示，當最後兩名病患從伊圖里省的治療中心出院時，醫護人員開心地跳舞慶祝。世界衛生組織（World Health Organization）秘書長譚德塞（Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus）表示，雖然疫情遠未結束，但每一個獲救的生命都值得慶祝。

paragraphs.en: Looking ahead, leaders are calling for faster action. Jean Kaseya, the head of the Africa CDC, emphasized that the response must move with stronger coordination and better political leadership. Health ministers from across Africa are planning a virtual summit to discuss how to work together more effectively. As the death toll nears 5,000, officials warn that the world must pay closer attention to the situation. Mohamed Janabi, a regional director for the World Health Organization, stated that they must reach people earlier and build trust within communities to stop the virus before it spreads further.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，各國領袖正呼籲採取更迅速的行動。非洲疾病管制暨預防中心負責人尚·卡塞亞（Jean Kaseya）強調，防疫工作必須具備更強的協調性與更好的政治領導。非洲各國衛生部長正計畫召開一場視訊高峰會，討論如何更有效地合作。隨著死亡人數逼近五千人，官員警告全球必須更密切關注此局勢。世界衛生組織區域主任穆罕默德·賈納比（Mohamed Janabi）表示，他們必須更早接觸民眾並建立社區信任，才能在病毒進一步擴散前將其阻斷。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To bear or support a burden or responsibility.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「搬運」實體物品，這裡指承擔責任。文中：As a result, local health workers are carrying most of the burden.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Being watched, checked, or kept under observation by authorities.
keyTerms.noteZh: 這裡指被衛生單位列入觀察名單的接觸者。文中：According to the Africa CDC, about 80% of new cases are coming from outside of monitored contacts.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To allow someone to leave a hospital after they have received treatment.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「釋放」或「排出」，這裡專指病人康復出院。文中：A recent video showed health workers dancing as the last two patients were discharged from a treatment center in Ituri province.

quiz.question: What is the primary reason medical professionals are struggling to treat the current Ebola outbreak?

options.A: The virus is spreading primarily through urban areas with poor infrastructure.
options.B: The specific strain of the virus involved currently lacks an approved vaccine or treatment.
options.C: International health organizations have completely withdrawn their support from the region.
options.D: The total number of cases has already exceeded the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段明確指出，此次疫情是由一種罕見的 Bundibugyo 病毒株引起，目前尚無核准的疫苗或特定治療方法。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章提到疫情擴散至偏遠地區（remote areas）而非僅限城市；選項 C 錯誤，文中僅提到國際合作較慢，並非撤出；選項 D 錯誤，文章第一段指出 2014-2016 年的疫情總病例數仍高於此次。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, why is the 'lack of trust' from local communities particularly dangerous for containment efforts?

options.A: It prevents the government from collecting taxes needed to fund the medical response.
options.B: It forces international health workers to work only in urban centers.
options.C: It causes new cases to go undetected because they occur outside of monitored contact groups.
options.D: It forces the World Health Organization to prioritize other African nations over the Congo.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第五段，民眾對醫療人員的不信任與恐懼導致他們不願配合，文章指出約 80% 的新病例來自監控接觸者之外，這意味著病毒在衛生當局無法追蹤的狀況下傳播。選項 A 與文章內容無關；選項 B 與 D 皆為錯誤推論，文章並未提到不信任感導致國際人員撤離或 WHO 改變優先順序。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does the author mean by saying local health workers are 'carrying most of the burden'?

options.A: They are physically transporting medical supplies across difficult terrain.
options.B: They are responsible for the majority of the work and pressure of the response.
options.C: They are the only ones who are currently infected with the virus.
options.D: They are suffering from the most severe physical symptoms of the disease.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。在文中 'carrying the burden' 是個慣用語，意指承擔重責大任或承受壓力。因為國際醫療人員參與度較低，當地的醫護人員必須承擔絕大多數的防疫工作。選項 A 將 'burden' 誤解為實體的重量；選項 C 與 D 則過度解讀，文中並未指明當地醫護人員的感染率或病情嚴重程度。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article regarding the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo?

options.A: The outbreak is primarily a political issue that can be solved by a virtual summit.
options.B: The virus has been successfully contained thanks to the efforts of local burial teams.
options.C: The crisis is a complex, multi-faceted challenge requiring better coordination and community trust.
options.D: The virus is less dangerous than previous outbreaks because it is spreading in remote areas.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。本文全面探討了疫情的嚴峻性，包括醫療技術限制、國際合作緩慢、社區不信任及資訊落差等挑戰，並強調未來需要更強的協調與建立信任。選項 A 將焦點縮小至政治層面；選項 B 與事實不符，疫情尚未結束；選項 D 錯誤，文中明確指出此次疫情是史上擴散最快的，絕非較不危險。
